title: Sentinel: Autonomous Intelligence Monitoring
content:
Sentinel is Crystal Ball's scheduled intelligence sweep. It normally runs every 30 minutes, collects snapshots across intelligence domains, evaluates alert rules, checks watchlists, and builds the historical record used by trend() and anomaly_scan().

Sentinel and the safety monitor are separate. The safety monitor normally runs every 15 minutes and checks feed health, algorithm drift, and quarantine state. Changing or disabling one schedule does not change the other.

On each Sentinel cycle, the configured runner queries sidecar endpoints, saves a timestamped snapshot, evaluates active alert rules, and checks watchlists for new activity. At least two snapshots are needed for trend analysis and three for anomaly detection.

Best practices: keep direct-source attribution, review missing capabilities before drawing conclusions, set meaningful alert rules, and let Sentinel accumulate history. Use get_monitor_status or crystalball monitor for safety-monitor state; do not treat a successful Sentinel sweep as proof that algorithm safeguards are healthy.
